author: Linnaeus, 1758

art.subject: Sedge Warbler (Acrocephalus schoenobaenus), adult (sexes alike) in autumn: crown dark brown with fine darker streaks, looking dark-capped, with no pale central crown stripe; a long, broad, creamy-white supercilium; dark brown eye-stripe; mantle and scapulars buff-brown with diffuse dark streaks; rump and uppertail coverts unstreaked warm tawny-brown; wings brown with darker-centred coverts and tertials; throat white; underparts whitish with a buff wash on the breast sides and flanks; tail plain dark brown; bill dark with a pale yellowish base to the lower mandible; dark eye; greyish-brown legs.
art.pose: perched on a reed stem, side view
art.scene: reed and sedge marsh in Korea during autumn migration in September, reeds turning buff; no people, buildings or text
art.build: A small, compact reed warbler, smaller than a sparrow and much smaller than an Oriental Reed Warbler, with a flat forehead and a rounded tail. Bill fairly short and straight, shorter than the head. Legs medium. Moderate primary projection; the folded wingtips reach a short way down the tail. Tail medium, rounded, plain, without white tips. Often climbs reed stems and perches in the open on top of vegetation.
avoid: Do not paint a pale buff stripe down the centre of the crown; that is Aquatic Warbler (Acrocephalus paludicola).
Do not give it white tail tips or a rufous, streaked rump (Pallas's Grasshopper Warbler).
Do not paint plain unstreaked upperparts (Black-browed Reed Warbler).
Do not paint a black line above the supercilium; the dark crown itself frames it.
